newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel-talks with France on budget pact continuing.
newsitem.headline: Waigel-talks with France on budget pact continuing.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday that talks with his French counterpart aimed at thrashing out details of a budget stability pact for monetary union would continue into the afternoon.

Waigel was meeting French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis at a Franco-German summit in the Bavarian town of Nuremberg. Most cabinet ministers of the two countries as well as the two countries' leaders are also holding talks.
In a break between the morning session and lunch, Waigel told reporters: "We are holding intensive discussions and will continue these this afternoon."

The so-called stability pact, originally proposed by Waigel as a means to ensure countries which enter European Economic and Monetary Union in 1999 keep their budget spending under control, is a key topic on the agenda for the talks.

Germany has found itself at odds with France -- and most of the rest of hte European Union -- in trying to set up a very strict budget pact which will mean semi-automatic penalties for countries whose governments overspend.
European economic and finance ministers failed to agree on a deal for the pact -- which will impose sanctions and then fines on offenders -- at a meeting in Brussels last week.
They will meet again on Thursday in a last-ditch attempt to agree the framework of a pact before an EU summit of government leaders and heads of state in Dublin which starts on Friday.

In response to a question, Waigel reiterated the need for a stability pact, adding that this was not simply an agreement needed to pacify the German public but would also help protect small countries within EMU from the actions of larger ones.
Noting that the Maastricht Treaty calls for countries to keep their spending under control long-term, he added that one main point of the stability pact was to make absolutely certain this occurred.
"We want to formulate this correctly at the right time so that there is no argument about it afterwards," he said.
